candidate.answerReason: The angles sum to 180° and differ by 40°, so the larger angle is 110°.

methods.label: Set up a linear equation
methods.explanation: Let this angle be \(x^\circ\). Then \(x-(180-x)=40\), \(2x=220\), and \(x=110\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the Grade 7 linear-pair property and a linear equation containing parentheses.

methods.label: Remove the excess
methods.explanation:
The adjacent supplementary angles total \(180^\circ\). Subtracting the larger angle's \(40^\circ\) excess leaves two equal amounts, so the smaller angle is
\[
\frac{180^\circ-40^\circ}{2}=70^\circ.
\]
The requested larger angle is therefore \(70^\circ+40^\circ=110^\circ\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary arithmetic to equalize the two quantities and requires no equation solving.
